reasons.reason: Marketing Hub Professional charges a mandatory one-time onboarding fee — $3,000 on Professional, $7,000 on Enterprise — before you send a single campaign.

picks.why: Its Starter plan runs a flat $97 a month with no forced setup charge; HighLevel's own done-with-you setup service is optional, not billed automatically at signup.
Bills strictly per seat starting at $24 a month on Lite, with a 14-day trial and no onboarding fee written into any of its four plans.

reasons.reason: Professional locks you into a 12-month term even when you pay monthly, and Enterprise sells on annual billing only, with no cancel-anytime option at either tier.

picks.why: Every edition is pay-as-you-go, and Zoho's own pricing FAQ says you can pay monthly or yearly and switch plans at any time with nothing to sign.
Month to month on every plan, including the ones with its deepest automation; you upgrade, downgrade or cancel from the dashboard rather than a new signed term.

reasons.reason: Marketing contacts above your tier bill immediately, and asking to exclude contacts from marketing status to bring the count back down only takes effect at your next renewal.

picks.why: Prices every edition strictly per user, with no contact-count tier to cross or wait out in the first place.
Ties its lead-and-deal capacity to the seats you already pay for instead of running a separate contact-tier meter on top of them.

reasons.reason: Marketing SMS exists only as an add-on to Professional or Enterprise, and only for U.S. numbers texting U.S. and Canadian recipients.

picks.why: Sells SMS on every plan, including its free one, with carrier fees already built into the per-segment rate rather than a feature gated behind a CRM tier.
Meters texting as usage on its $97 floor plan once a one-time A2P 10DLC registration is done, instead of holding SMS back for an $890-a-month tier.

reasons.reason: Starter's email automation stops at 10 automated actions, so a small team building real multi-step workflows has to jump straight to Professional's much larger monthly base.

picks.why: Includes marketing automation and a light CRM on its cheapest paid plan, not a feature held back for a pricier tier the way Starter's cap works.

reasons.reason: Every Core Seat is billed at your highest edition across every hub, so adding one pricier Sales or Service Hub tier quietly raises what your existing marketing seats cost too.

picks.why: Prices seats on the CRM edition alone; there's no second product whose tier could push an existing seat's price up.
Every plan, including Free, includes unlimited staff accounts, so there's no per-seat price for a second product to inflate in the first place.
